output:
**What I found:** The document database doesn't fit your domain. Switch to one relational database now, before the first customer, and don't wait (the record calls this MIGRATE). The deciding fact is that your code already contains every workaround that points to a relational domain on a document store, and production holds no real customer data yet, so the switch will never be cheaper than it is today.

**Why it matters:** If you switch now, you rewrite the persistence layer and delete the hand-written uniqueness checks, conflict retries, application-side joins and old-shape readers, with no live data to move. If you wait, every customer's data adds a staged migration, keeps the readers alive, and the store keeps taking about one commit in eight.

**Do this first:**
1. Check that every environment, including production, holds only test or seed data. Then write the store decision record (forcing need: the invariants that span entities and the reporting joins) wherever your project keeps decisions.
2. Build the relational store behind a port your team owns. Run the walking skeleton on it: sign-in, deploy and rollback, a restore drill, erasure of one person's data, a cross-tenant read that gets refused, and your hardest report.
3. Then decide on compute and sign-in. Both depend on the new store (records below).

**What I did not check:**
- This folder isn't a git repository and has no application code, so I couldn't count commits. Run `git log --since=6.months --name-only --format= | grep -c <store-path>` against `git rev-list --count --since=6.months HEAD` in the product repo.
- I didn't search for the workaround patterns in the code. Grep for retry-on-conflict, uniqueness lookups and shape-version readers.
- I didn't confirm that production holds no real data. Run a row or document count per collection in each environment.
- I didn't check whether the sign-in service issues standard OIDC tokens or is tied to the document platform. Read the backend's auth configuration.

```text
Mode:            Review (workarounds accumulating; first real data not yet entered)
Component:       Document database
Door:            ONE-WAY
Status:          INHERITED (starter template default; no decision recorded)
Forcing need:    none found
Profile:         Domain shape: employers, employees, roles, assessments, reports; uniqueness,
                 referential integrity, cross-entity joins -> relational.
                 Access: reports joining all entities. Scale: tens of small tenants -> one node.
                 Data lifecycle, residency, cost: GAP
Evidence:        As reported by you, NOT VERIFIED: hand-written uniqueness checks, write-conflict
                 retries, joins in application code, readers for old document shapes,
                 ~1 in 8 commits touching the store
Verdict:         MIGRATE
Tripwires:       n/a for the old store; for the new one: store-touching commit share > 10% per
                 quarter, owner = tech lead, checked at the quarterly fit review
Reversal cost:   Low now (persistence rewrite, seed data only); rises with every tenant's real rows
Handoff:         evolutionary-database-design (only if any environment holds data worth keeping)
Next action:     Confirm no real data, then define the relational schema with uniqueness and
                 foreign-key constraints in the database
```

```text
Mode:            Review (store change alters compute fit)
Component:       Serverless backend
Door:            ONE-WAY
Status:          INHERITED
Forcing need:    none found
Profile:         Scale: tens of small tenants, likely idle most of the time (scale-to-zero may
                 pay). Workload shape, cost envelope, operability: GAP
Evidence:        NOT VERIFIED. Serverless plus relational brings a connection-limit and
                 cold-start risk
Verdict:         DEFER (missing: workload shape, cost envelope, a relational skeleton run)
Tripwires:       DB connection exhaustion or p95 cold start above the agreed budget during the
                 skeleton run, owner = tech lead
Reversal cost:   Moderate; lower if handlers stay thin behind the store port
Handoff:         requirements-grounding (fill the workload and cost dimensions)
Next action:     Run the skeleton's hardest report from a serverless function against the new
                 database, through a pooler or HTTP driver
```

```text
Mode:            Review (store change may drag identity with it)
Component:       Platform-managed sign-in
Door:            ONE-WAY
Status:          INHERITED
Forcing need:    none found
Profile:         Identity: employer admins and employees; federation needs: GAP.
                 Erasure across store and identity provider: GAP
Evidence:        NOT VERIFIED
Verdict:         DEFER (missing: token standard, where the user store lives, where roles are
                 enforced)
Tripwires:       Authorization logic found in platform rules rather than the app, or erasure
                 that cannot reach the identity provider, owner = tech lead, checked in the
                 skeleton erasure path
Reversal cost:   Rises sharply once real users exist (password and credential migration)
Handoff:         none until the skeleton runs
Next action:     Confirm the provider issues standard OIDC tokens and that roles live in the

```
